Package com.egradx.core.utils

Class EncryptionUtil

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.core.utils.EncryptionUtil
public final class EncryptionUtil extends Object
Envelope encryption for secrets stored at rest — provider passwords, API tokens and the like.

Each secret is encrypted with its own random data-encryption key (DEK). The DEK is then encrypted with a key-encryption key (KEK) derived from a passphrase the application holds outside the database (egradx.security.crypto.passphrase), using a random salt stored alongside. A database dump therefore yields nothing without the passphrase, and rotating the passphrase means re-wrapping DEKs rather than re-encrypting every secret.

The scheme matches ikon-v9's CredentialsEncryptionUtils, which is where the algorithm and iteration count come from.

Ciphertexts are Base64 of nonce || ciphertext-with-GCM-tag, so they fit a plain text column. GCM authenticates as well as encrypts: a tampered or wrongly-keyed value fails to decrypt with an exception rather than yielding garbage.
